Article Title: 'Didn't want Mamata to contest another election': Suvendu Adhikari on why he kept Bhabanipur seat
Article Text:
शुभेंदु अधिकारी और ममता बनर्जी

NEW DELHI: Explaining his decision to vacate his Nandigram stronghold and retain Bhabanipur, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday that vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee , another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll and return to the state assembly.Adhikari, who won both seats in the West Bengal assembly elections in April, defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur. He had also defeated the then chief minister in Nandigram in the 2021 assembly elections, following which Banerjee contested a bypoll from Bhabanipur and won.The chief minister also took a dig at his predecessor, suggesting that she should retire from electoral politics given her age.“Had I vacated Bhabanipur, the person (Mamata Banerjee) I had defeated twice would have got another opportunity to contest an election. I did not want to give her that opportunity. I had trounced her in Bhabanipur, and I would urge her not to contest elections any more. You have already crossed 75 years of age. There is no need to enter the electoral fray any further. You should take rest at home,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying.He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs following their victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls earlier this month.The BJP leader also sought to reassure people in Nandigram, who he said were “upset” with him for leaving the constituency. He asserted that he would fulfil his commitments to them through Hasirani Rath, the newly elected MLA from Nandigram.“The people of Nandigram were upset with me for leaving the constituency, but I have explained my decision to them. I had to leave Nandigram for this reason. The people have now elected Hasirani Rath with a margin of 1.22 lakh votes. I will fulfil my promise to them through her,” he added.Hasirani Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari’s aide who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the West Bengal assembly election results were declared. The BJP came to power in the state for the first time, ending the Trinamool Congress’s 15-year rule.Turning to the murder of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari alleged that his aide was killed because of his association with him, describing it as a “supari”, or contract killing.“Chandranath was murdered simply because he was my aide. The CBI has arrested seven people, including the shooters and contract killers. What remains to be established is where the Rs 2 crore ‘supari’ for the contract killing came from. Was it Camac Street, Kalighat or Diamond Harbour? Once that is known, the investigation will be complete,” he said.Adhikari appeared to be referring to Camac Street, associated with the office of Trinamool Congress national general secretary and Mamata's nephew Abhishek Banerjee; Kalighat, where Mamata Banerjee resides; and Diamond Harbour, the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Abhishek Banerjee.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll and return to the state assembly. He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs.

Article Title: Nepal faces days of rain, snow and storms as Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in India
Article Text:
Cyclone Arnab (Representational Image)

NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recording up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm’s impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall from Thursday.The Nepal Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecasting Division said the country was currently experiencing the partial influence of westerly winds, with the approaching cyclone expected to bring widespread precipitation and a risk of heavy rain and snowfall through the weekend.“The country is currently under the partial influence of westerly winds. In addition, the country is expected to come under the influence of Cyclone ‘Arnab’, developed over the Bay of Bengal, from Kartik 12 (Thursday),” the department said in its latest bulletin.Weather conditions remained relatively clear in the Himalayan and hilly regions on Wednesday morning, although fog and mist affected parts of the Terai, valleys and river basins.The department forecast increasing cloud cover and scattered precipitation from Wednesday afternoon, with conditions becoming more unsettled overnight. Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces are among the areas expected to experience rain, while snowfall is possible in Himalayan regions.The risk is forecast to increase on Thursday night, when thunderstorms and lightning could accompany rain and snowfall. Heavy precipitation is possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, while some areas of Lumbini could also receive heavy rainfall.Friday and Saturday are expected to bring the most widespread impacts. The department warned that heavy rain or snowfall could affect several provinces, with isolated locations facing the possibility of very heavy precipitation.Its Friday forecast states, “Mostly cloudy throughout the country. Light to moderate rain or snowfall accompanied by thunder and lightning is possible at most places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces and at many places in Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces.”The expected combination of westerly winds and moisture associated with Cyclone Arnab could increase the risk of flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in vulnerable hilly regions. Heavy snowfall could also create hazardous conditions in high-altitude areas.Meanwhile, in India, at least three people died in cyclone Arnab-related incidents in Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday. South Coast Railway (SCoR) cancelled 57 trains and rescheduled 15 others as a precautionary measure. However, officials quoted by ANI said the cyclone had weakened from a very severe to a severe cyclonic storm after moving over land, and was expected to weaken further. Four additional NDRF teams were deployed to Andhra Pradesh.
Article Summary: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles. Some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have recorded up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm's impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for rain, thunderstorms and snowfall.

Article Title: MLC election results: Congress faces setback across 4 states; state-wise results and key wins
Article Text:
The biennial elections for these Graduate and Teacher constituencies across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, and Maharashtra were held via ballot papers on October 23, 2026, with counting beginning on October 27, 2026.

Here is a state-wise look at the latest results and counting trends.

Karnataka (4 seats): BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four, Congress draws blank

Uttar Pradesh (11 seats): BJP wins four seats, SP secures two

Bihar (8 seats): Jan Suraaj opens account, RJD defeats BJP veteran

Maharashtra (5 seats): BJP's Sudhakar Kohale leads Congress in Nagpur

NEW DELHI: Congress faced a major setback in the legislative council elections on Wednesday, failing to secure a victory in the seats declared so far across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra, even as counting continued in several constituencies.The BJP -JD(S) alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, where the ruling Congress drew a blank despite having a majority in the state Assembly. The BJP retained three constituencies, while the JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins, while in Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its legislative council account by defeating the Congress. The RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP.Counting for 28 legislative council seats across Uttar Pradesh (11), Bihar (8), Maharashtra (5) and Karnataka (4) began on Tuesday following polling on October 23. The elections were held for graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, with results declared for several seats and counting continuing in others.The BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats in Karnataka, dealing a setback to the ruling Congress.The BJP retained the North-East Teachers’, South-East Graduates’ and West Graduates’ constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes in Bengaluru Teachers’. Ranganath secured 10,810 votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.BJP’s Shashil G Namoshi retained North-East Teachers’ by 3,297 votes, securing his fifth victory from the constituency with 15,596 votes against Congress candidate Sharanappa Mattur’s 12,299.In South-East Graduates’, BJP candidate K M Suresh defeated Congress nominee Shashi Hulikunte Mutt by 23,098 votes. Sitting BJP MLC S V Sankanur retained West Graduates’, defeating Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai by 9,323 votes.The results marked a clean sweep for the opposition alliance, with the Congress failing to win a single seat despite campaigning by chief minister D K Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and other senior leaders.However, the results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government or significantly alter the balance of power in the 75-member Legislative Council.The BJP won four of the 11 Uttar Pradesh legislative council seats, while the SP secured two, according to the latest confirmed results.The BJP retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat, where Hari Singh Dhillon defeated SP’s Danish Akhtar by 17,676 votes. It also won the Lucknow Teachers’ seat, with Umesh Dwivedi defeating SP candidate Sushil Kumar by 6,992 votes. The party also won both the Meerut Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies.The SP won the Varanasi Teachers’ seat through Lal Bihari Yadav and the Agra-Aligarh Teachers’ seat, where Akash Agrawal defeated BJP nominee Hari Kishore Tiwari.In the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’ constituency, SP candidate Mansingh Yadav secured 27,157 votes after the fifth round, against BJP candidate Ashok Rathore’s 7,648. SP candidates were also leading in the Varanasi and Lucknow Graduates’ constituencies.BJP candidate Manvendra Singh was leading in the Agra-Aligarh Graduates’ constituency.In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ seat, BJP candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi received 11,881 votes against independent candidate Rajiv Yadav’s 11,415 after the final round, though disputes arose over the counting process. The SP alleged irregularities and boycotted the counting process.Meanwhile, an additional commissioner was removed following a candidate’s complaint after 52 more votes were found in a ballot box from Mau than recorded in the official data.The Bihar legislative council elections delivered several upsets, with the BJP, RJD, Jan Suraaj Party and an Independent winning one Teachers’ constituency each.Jan Suraaj Party candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers’ constituency, officials said on Wednesday. The victory marked the party’s first win in the Bihar Legislative Council.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut Teachers’ seat, defeating independent candidate Bhushan Kumar Jha.In another major result, RJD candidate Dr Sanjeev Kumar defeated the BJP’s veteran MLC Nawal Kishore Yadav in the Patna Teachers’ constituency, ending his long hold on the seat.Independent candidate Rahul Raj also defeated sitting MLC Afaq Ahmed in the Saran Teachers’ constituency.Meanwhile, JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar was leading RJD candidate Dilip Rai in Patna Graduates’, with reports indicating a victory for the JD(U) leader, although the official result was awaited in the latest update.Counting continued in the remaining Graduates’ constituencies.The polls will decide the fate of 90 candidates in four graduates’ constituencies and 60 candidates in four teachers’ constituencies. Turnout stood at 82.85% in teachers’ constituencies and 53.42% in graduates’ seats.Counting continued for five Maharashtra legislative council seats, with BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale leading sitting Congress MLC Abhijit Wanjari by 4,294 votes in the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency after the second round.Kohale secured 60,924 votes against Wanjari’s 56,630, while independent candidate Nitesh Karale received 24,249 votes. A total of 15,106 votes were declared invalid.None of the candidates had reached the winning quota of 75,438 votes, with the final outcome dependent on further counting and the transfer of preferential votes.In the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik was also leading as counting continued.The polls, held on October 23, saw 182 candidates contesting across three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies. The results are being watched amid rebel candidates, alliance differences and efforts by the BJP-led Mahayuti and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi to consolidate support.The terms of the sitting members are due to end on December 6, and the election process is scheduled to be completed by October 31.
Article Summary: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four legislative council seats in Karnataka. RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP. Results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government.

Article Title: BJP fields Hardeep Singh Puri as its candidate for Rajya Sabha bypoll from MP

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party BJP ) on Wednesday nominated senior leader and Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri for the Rajya Sabha bypoll in Madhya Pradesh.According to an official press release issued from the BJP's central office on Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, the party's Central Election Committee cleared Puri's name for the Upper House seat."The Central Election Committee of the Bharatiya Janata Party has given its approval to the name for the upcoming Rajya Sabha bye-election 2026 in Madhya Pradesh: Hardeep Singh Puri," the statement read.The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.The Election Commission announced the schedule for the bypoll on October 22.According to the schedule, the notification for the election will be issued on October 26. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny will take place on November 3. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5.Polling will be held on November 12 from 9am to 4pm, followed by counting at 5pm on the same day. The entire election process is scheduled to be completed by November 16, the poll panel said.Puri, a former diplomat who later entered politics, currently serves as a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's government and holds the petroleum and natural gas portfolio.
Article Summary: Hardeep Singh Puri is a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government. The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.

Article Title: 'Failed to establish presence': BJP takes 'ballot paper' jibe at Rahul after Congress draws blank in MLC polls
Article Text:
BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt

Karnataka: BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats

Uttar Pradesh: BJP vs SP battle

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday targeted Congress over the results of MLC elections across four states, claiming that the grand old party has "failed to make its presence felt" in the polls conducted using ballot papers.The BJP's strong remarks came amid Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's repeated allegations against the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities.Addressing a presser, BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said, "The message is clear... the Congress party has failed to make its presence felt in these (MLC ) elections. More importantly, these elections were conducted using ballot boxes and ballot papers, yet the Congress failed to establish its presence. To put it in terms that the Congress leaders would understand better, the party has failed to make its very existence felt. This makes it clear that the Congress party lacks the ability to secure public support or the support of the voters concerned in any election, whether it is conducted using EVMs or ballot papers."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi launched attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi as the BJP and its NDA allies registered wins in the MLC elections.He said, "The Congress party should understand that Rahul Gandhi, after spending nearly two weeks sightseeing and enjoying himself, has now returned to the limelight and is talking about launching a movement that could create problems for the Indian economy. He must understand that neither the public nor the MLAs are with him. The Congress party must understand that public support is earned through hard work, not through sightseeing and leisure trips.""Our national president, Nitin Nabin, is travelling to Uttar Pradesh, while Amit Shah is in Punjab. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi had disappeared from the scene and was wandering around 'Champa'. 'Champa' was the ancient name of Vietnam. After that, he expects to receive public support. I would therefore like to tell the Congress party... give up your habit of avoiding hard work, and the slogan of 'vote theft' will automatically disappear," Sudhanshu Trivedi added.The BJP's remarks came as the party and its allies registered wins in several Legislative Council constituencies, while the Congress faced setbacks in Karnataka and Bihar.In Karnataka, the BJP took a jibe at chief minister DK Shivakumar after the opposition BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four seats in the state's Legislative Council elections, leaving the ruling Congress without a win.The BJP's Karnataka unit posted on X, saying, "DK, it’s done, bro!"It added, "NDA SWEEPS 4/4 Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies in the MLC elections!"The BJP retained the North-East Teachers', South-East Graduates' and West Graduates' constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers' seat from the Congress.In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra, while the BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats, with counting under way in the remaining constituencies, officials said on Wednesday.SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of resorting to alleged electoral malpractice to win the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections. He claimed that irregularities in the counting process had exposed a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi.In a post on X, Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders, their associates and officials had colluded to manipulate the counting process. He claimed that the alleged treatment of Tripathi had angered teachers and his community, and vowed that his party would oppose what he described as injustice and harassment.The BJP has denied no specific allegations in the information provided.In Bihar, the Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party opened its account in the Legislative Council elections after its candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers' constituency, officials said on Wednesday.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh had on Tuesday defeated his nearest rival, Independent nominee Bhushan Kumar Jha, to win the Tirhut Teachers' constituency.Counting was still under way for some Legislative Council seats, officials said.
Article Summary: BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt. BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats in Karnataka. Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra. BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats.

Article Title: 'Taking down Instagram accounts won't make questions disappear': Abhijeet Dipke accuses Centre of digital crackdown
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke

NEW DELHI : Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.On Wednsday, in a post on X, Dipke wrote, “The Instagram crackdown is not going to work!“The government is taking down thousands of posts and accounts every day, but it seems to be missing a fundamental point.“Instagram is just a platform where people are raising their questions. The reasons behind those questions exist far beyond social media, and taking down accounts won't make them disappear,” Dipke wrote, warning that the alleged censorship could further erode trust among the very people the government is supposed to answer to.His remarks come amid wider scrutiny of online content restrictions and freedom of expression. Activists and political groups have raised concerns over account suspensions and takedown directives, including those reportedly issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.According to PTI, social media platforms including Meta and X have been asked by the Centre to restrict posts and handles raising questions on youth unemployment, governance, and public infrastructure.Critics argue that restricting online content does not address underlying concerns over unemployment, examination paper leaks, governance and public infrastructure.The issue has also reached the courts. On October 27, the Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre and the concerned department on a petition challenging the withholding of the Instagram handle @bring_back__ballot in India.The account is associated with the “Bring Back Ballot” initiative of Mission Save Constitution and advocate Mehmood Pracha, its national convenor.The petition stated that the handle was withheld on October 10, the day organisers held a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. It displayed the message: “Account not available in India. This is because we complied with a legal request to restrict this content.”The petitioners alleged, “No notice, hearing, reasons or copy of any order was ever furnished to the Petitioners.”The initiative advocated a return to paper ballots under the slogan “EVM Hatao Desh Bachao”. The petition said organisers had informed Delhi Police about the protest on October 9.Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice and sought the Centre’s response. Central Government Standing Counsel Ashish Dixit accepted notice on behalf of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the designated officer. Advocate Amee Rana accepted notice for Meta Platforms.The matter is listed for hearing on November 6, when the court is expected to consider the petition further.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.

Article Title: 'We don't want a fight': Delhi traders' body writes to Rahul Gandhi again over November 1 rally
Article Text:
Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi (File photo)

NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali over fears that the gathering could disrupt business in several major markets.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), which has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales, also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred.In the letter, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted an opportunity to put forward their concerns about the rally, which is expected to draw around 10 lakh people."We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy," Goyal said.The traders' body also proposed that it would withdraw its protest if Gandhi could convince its representatives that the rally would bring more customers and boost business. However, if traders were able to convince him that the event would result in losses, they wanted him to agree to postpone it until after Diwali.Wednesday's letter was the second sent by CTI to Gandhi within four days. The organisation had first approached the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha on October 24, seeking postponement of the rally to prevent disruptions during one of the busiest periods for Delhi's markets.According to CTI, at least 20 markets within a 1-5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan could be affected by the expected turnout.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj.Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market are also among the commercial areas identified by the traders' body.The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori" and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition alliance has called the November 1 rally to step up pressure on the government and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The rally follows a series of demonstrations by opposition parties over the electoral-roll revision exercise.On October 12, opposition leaders, including Gandhi, joined activists and civil society members in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route near the Supreme Court in Delhi. A joint petition challenging the SIR was also filed.A day later, Gandhi hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his residence. Following the meeting, the opposition alliance vowed to continue its campaign and take the fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales. It also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred. The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori"

Article Title: UP MLC polls: SP secures Varanasi and Agra seat, BJP wins 4
Article Text:
Lal Bihari Yadav secured the Varanasi Teachers' seat





LUCKNOW: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers’ seat, while the Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers’ constituencies as counting for 11 MLC seats continued.In the Meerut-Saharanpur Graduates’ constituency, BJP’s sitting MLC Dinesh Goyal retained his seat, defeating SP candidate Pramod Singh Bhati by 12,855 votes. BJP’s Shrichand Sharma also retained the Meerut Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Nitin Tomar by 13,241 votes.BJP’s Hari Singh Dhillon retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Haji Mohammad Danish Akhtar.In another victory for the BJP, sitting MLC Umesh Dwivedi retained the Lucknow Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Sushil Kumar (Baba). UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary congratulated Dwivedi on his victory in a post on X on Wednesday morning, expressing confidence that he would continue working for the development of the education sector.Meanwhile, SP’s sitting MLC Lal Bihari Yadav retained the Varanasi Teachers’ constituency, defeating BJP candidate Pramod Mishra by approximately 4,900 votes.In the Agra Teachers’ constituency, SP candidate Akash Agrawal emerged victorious, defeating BJP candidate Hari Kishore Tiwari. Agrawal had won the same seat as an Independent in 2020. His latest victory means he has retained the constituency, this time as an SP candidate.In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, BJP’s Dhruv Tripathi was leading by a narrow margin of 110 votes in the last available update, with Independent candidate Rajeev Yadav and SP candidate Sanjayan also in contention.Polling for five Graduates’ and six Teachers’ constituencies was held on October 23, with 152 candidates in the fray. Repolling at three polling stations in the Agra Teachers’ constituency took place on Monday following orders from the Election Commission.Final results from the remaining constituencies were awaited.
Article Summary: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers' seat. Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers' constituencies.

Article Title: Omar inducts 4 ministers, dissent spills over in NC ranks
Article Text:
File photo: Omar Abdullah

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah ’s cabinet expansion triggered open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in National Conference after four ministers were inducted Tuesday. MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi, who had expected a berth until the last moment, broke down and other legislators accused the party brass of shutting them out. Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath to Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including Omar. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region — deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana.Legislators alleged a lack of internal democracy. “I am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,” Larmi said.Independent MLA Muzaffar Iqbal Khan, who supports NC, boycotted the ceremony, alleging discrimination against Poonch-Rajouri. Khan plans to convene six independent MLAs supporting NC-led govt to discuss their next move.Supporters of MLA Mubarak Gul protested at the party headquarters, while Nazir Ahmad Khan was said to be unhappy with the expansion. Health minister Sakina Itoo dismissed the protests.The 90-member assembly allows a maximum of nine ministers, including the CM. Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, with five ministers. Three berths remained vacant for nearly two years.An NC legislator said the next three months would test whether the party brass could contain the anger. “The way the expansion was carried out has humiliated party legislators. There seems to be no democracy within the party,” he said.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah ’s cabinet expansion triggered open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in National Conference. MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi, who had expected a berth until the last moment, broke down and other legislators accused the party brass of shutting them out.Independent MLA Muzaffar Iqbal Khan, who supports NC, boycotted the ceremony, alleging discrimination against Poonch-Rajouri.

Article Title: Mercedes crash: Kochi police commissioner removed from post after accident involving judge’s minor son; 4 cops suspended
Article Text:
Kochi City Police Commissioner Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar has been transferred, along with the suspension of four personnel.





Kochi: The Keralam govt has removed S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar as Kochi City District Police Chief amid mounting allegations of police lapses in the handling of the Cheranalloor fatal car crash case, in which a 55-year-old man was killed by a speeding luxury car allegedly driven by the 17-year-old son of an additional judge.Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan signed the order on Wednesday , acting on a recommendation from the Home Department. R. Nishanthini, currently serving as IGP (South Zone), is likely to succeed Kumar, who is yet to be given a new posting.The removal follows the suspension on Tuesday of four officers attached to the Cheranalloor police station. The suspended officers are station house officer and sub-inspector Viswajith V S, circle inspector Syam Kumar K S, grade ASI Manoj K T and senior civil police officer Arun Joshy. Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was reportedly heading home when the accident occurred around 2.20 am.Home minister Ramesh Chennithala had told the assembly that there had been serious police lapses and that he had personally reprimanded the director general of police after learning that the FIR had not initially included the charge of culpable homicide. A team of officers led by ADGP (law and order) P Vijayan visited the accident site and the victim’s family in Kochi on Tuesday, as directed by the minister.Vijayan held discussions with senior Kochi city police officers, including commissioner Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, for nearly two hours on Tuesday. He also visited the accident site at Maraparambu on Container Road and briefly spoke to a watchman who was present at the spot. Both Ramesh and Vijayan said the law would take its course irrespective of persons involved.Addressing media, Vijayan had said that the police had already moved the court seeking to revoke the bail granted to the juvenile by the concerned magistrate. When asked about the possibility of an arrest of the judge, as he was arrayed as an accused, he said that it was a matter that involved multiple legal formalities, including obtaining the requisite permission from the judiciary.Meanwhile, the arrival of a separate team from the state capital is widely interpreted as a sign of the authorities' dissatisfaction with the city police's handling of the investigation.The family of the victim had also staged another protest at the station on Monday night, but called it off after Ramesh assured a fair investigation. They had warned that they would resume the protest if their demands were not met by 4 pm on Tuesday.Meanwhile, an overnight search at the judge's apartment in Aluva continued for several hours until Wednesday morning. Police have collected CCTV footage from the premises and seized documents relating to the luxury car involved in the crash and a premium motorcycle. Footage purportedly showing the car being driven out of the apartment had earlier circulated widely on social media.The police had initially registered a case against the minor driver under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to rash driving and causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. The teenager was subsequently released on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.Police had evidence that the car had travelled at over 100 kmph sometime before the accident, and Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and charges for speeding were added. The juvenile who was sent home on Monday morning was later picked up again after an additional section was added.
Article Summary: S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar has been transferred, along with the suspension of four personnel. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan signed the order on Wednesday, acting on a recommendation from the Home Department. The removal follows the suspension on Tuesday of four officers attached to the Cheranalloor police station.

Article Title: Delhi to Haridwar in 90 minutes? What Nitin Gadkari said
Article Text:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari announced a new road project connecting Delhi to Haridwar. (Pic Credit: PTI)

Expressways to open up new economic opportunities

The journey from Delhi to Haridwar may soon become significantly shorter, with a new road project scheduled to open next month, union road hransport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari said on Tuesday. Once operational, the route could bring travel time down to around 90 minutes.Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on ‘Highways of India’s Future: Smart, Safe and Sustainable’, Gadkari said the expansion of the country’s road network was making religious destinations more accessible while supporting tourism and job creation.Pointing to the recently opened Delhi-Dehradun corridor, the minister said the journey between the two cities, which earlier took about seven hours, could now be completed in roughly two hours.He said the upcoming Delhi-Haridwar project would further improve access to one of the country’s prominent pilgrimage destinations, according to ET.Gadkari also cited road development work in Ayodhya and Maharashtra, including the Pandharpur Palkhi Marg projects, which are intended to make journeys easier for devotees. He said infrastructure development was being undertaken across regions, with roads, tunnels and bridges being built in the Northeast, Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country.Gadkari said greenfield expressways could bring regions with limited economic opportunities closer to major business centres, helping expand development beyond established urban hubs.The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, he said, would improve access for rural areas, aspirational districts and tribal regions. In Haryana, the project is expected to benefit aspirational districts, while Alwar, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur and Bundi in Rajasthan are among the areas that could gain from improved road links.He also pointed to Ratlam and Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh and Dahod in Gujarat, highlighting the potential for better connectivity to encourage economic activity in tribal districts.Stressing the importance of the Delhi-Mumbai route, Gadkari said stronger links between the national capital and Mumbai were crucial, given the latter’s position as the country’s economic hub.The minister said infrastructure spending has benefits beyond the construction of roads, as projects generate employment and increase demand for cement, steel and construction equipment.He added that improved connectivity could lower transportation costs and make the movement of goods and people more efficient. These gains, he said, could benefit businesses, tourism and the development of towns.Describing infrastructure as a key driver of economic growth, Gadkari said every 100 invested in the sector could produce an economic impact of 325.“If we spend 100 on infrastructure, the impact on the economy comes to 325. GDP is also going to increase,” he said.Gadkari added that the government was continuing to focus on expressways and greenfield highways to improve links between regions, strengthen economic activity and support development across India.

Article Title: Karnataka MLC polls: Big setback for DK Shivakumar as BJP-led NDA wins all 4 seats
Article Text: BENGALURU: In a major setback to the ruling Congress and chief minister D K Shivakumar, the BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, sweeping both teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies.The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated Congress veteran and five-time MLC Puttanna in the Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi registered his fifth victory in the North-East Teachers’ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. Namoshi secured 15,596 first-preference votes against Mattur’s 12,299.Counting concluded at Kalaburagi, where around 30,253 voters had exercised their franchise. Of the votes counted, 28,380 were valid, while 1,873 were rejected.In the graduates’ constituencies, BJP candidates SV Sankanur and KM Suresh also emerged victorious, completing the NDA’s clean sweep of all four seats.In the West Graduates’ constituency, Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory, defeating Congress rival Mohan Limbikai.In the other graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate KM Suresh won the seat, ensuring that the NDA did not concede any ground to the ruling party in the elections.This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3. In the June 18 elections to seven council seats from the MLAs’ quota, Congress won five seats and the BJP secured two. However, the ruling party failed to replicate that performance in the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies.Ranganath won the Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency on his third attempt, defeating Puttanna by 908 votes. He secured 10,810 first-preference votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.Ranganath had lost to Puttanna in the 2022 and 2024 elections. This time, he capitalised on a sympathy wave to secure victory. Puttanna had contested as a BJP candidate in 2022 before switching to Congress for the 2024 by-election.
Article Summary: The BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23. The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate. This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3.

NEW DELHI: It began as a regular meeting. But the senior bureaucrats who had gathered at a performance review meeting on Tuesday were in for a surprise — and not a particularly pleasant one, even though the point was made with a generous dose of humour.Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan unveiled a presentation on 12 types of bureaucrats, which is believed to have left many present at the meeting squirming. Among the types listed by Somanathan were officers who ask women colleagues to come a bit too close for comfort to show them a document; those who throw files and speak rudely; and those who call in staff on Saturdays, then arrive late themselves.Other entries included officers who call meetings after 7pm, sit on files, or send ministers decisions they could take themselves. Each type was accompanied by a cartoon, in many cases work by TOI’s legendary cartoonist R K Laxman.Apart from cartoons and indirect criticism, there was a quantitative component to the meeting too — the secretaries of various govt departments were ranked on various performance parameters.The CabSec’s broader message, officials said, was about running better meetings and making the workplace more conducive to getting things done.He also informed officers about the Centre’s plans to roll out the next round of reforms, Deregulation 3.0, from Jan, aiming to cut red tape, simplify compliance and improve the ease of doing business.At a meeting of senior bureaucrats on Tuesday, Union cabinet secretary T V Somanathan urged faster inter-ministerial consultations. Union finance and commerce ministries, Somanathan is learnt to have said, should send their views promptly to avoid any delays. The cabinet secretary also noted that officers’ performance scores often cluster close to 10 on a scale of 1 to 10, leaving the ranking system with little room to demarcate the stars from the merely satisfactory.Meanwhile, the department of food and public distribution took the opportunity to flag that around 1 lakh railway employees have ration cards allowing them to receive free foodgrain under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.Calling it a disciplinary issue, Somanathan directed Railway Board chairman Satish Kumar to ensure that the employees surrender their ration cards.Last month, the food department had written to the cabinet secretary about ration cards being used to establish family identity under Ayushman Bharat’s Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) scheme, even though they are not a formal eligibility requirement.
Article Summary: Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan unveiled a presentation on 12 types of bureaucrats. Article Title: SC: Cannot let pharma industry ‘run amok’ in name of free market
Article Text:
SC questioned the Centre over pharma companies pricing medicines at over 1,000% of cost, saying the industry can't "run amok" in the name of free market.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday said the pharma industry cannot be allowed to “run amok” in the name of free market to fix the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines at an exponentially high level, which in some cases happens to be over 1,000% of the price at which they are sold to retailers.Expressing anguish over the suffering of the common man who had to pay the price, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the court is “pained by the loot” and repeatedly asked Centre to explain the rationale behind allowing a high MRP and who ultimately benefits from the policy. It reserved its order on plea to bring all non-patented medicines and medical consumables under price control mechanism like scheduled drugs.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, who had to face a volley of questions from the bench, tried to convince the court that govt was aware of the problem and that was why it recently decided to cap the price of anti-cancer drugs. But the court responded that govt “woke up” only after it intervened and passed harsh observations on the prevailing system.She, however, said the deliberation was already on and SC’s intervention expedited it.“People are living in a daydream that someday they will benefit from the drugs prices control order (DPCO)... The policy is only to give benefit to the corporate. We are thinking from the point of view of poor patients,” SC observed. Bhati, thereafter, submitted that medicine prices in India are among the lowest in the world due to free market and govt cannot take control of the entire pharma market, but the bench told her, “You are either not aware about the problem or not keen to solve the problem... Why is the entire system working for the benefit of few people?”“Ordinarily, where there is substantial competition, there is no need to regulate prices. It is not that the govt has left the market unregulated but the complete control of the market is not feasible,” Bhati said, adding that the issue pertains to economic policy and commerce and the court should desist from interfering. Not convinced by this, the bench said, “Should they (pharma companies) be allowed to run amok? What is the justification for the difference in prices? You are not able to come with an answer. We have asked you 30 times. Do not talk about control... You are talking about economic policy and commerce. Is commerce more important than the life of citizens and be given precedence?”
Article Summary: Supreme Court said the pharma industry cannot be allowed to “run amok’ in the name of free market. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta repeatedly asked Centre to explain the rationale behind allowing a high MRP. It reserved its order on plea to bring all non-patented medicines and medical consumables under price control mechanism.

Article Title: A decade after liquor ban, Bihar faces a new drug question: What the numbers reveal
Article Text:
NCB destroyed 1,170.15 kg of seized narcotics worth Rs 4.54 crore in Patna, Bihar, across four cases to prevent their recirculation in September (Credit: NCB's X)

Does Bihar have a new drug problem?

Where are the drugs coming from?

Cops suggest that drugs in Bihar enters from multiple states

Is the trade limited to transportation?

Is Bihar seeing a rise in consumption or a rise in detection?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Does Bihar have a new drug problem?

Punjab is set to go to polls in 2027, and the BJP, seeking to form its first government in the state, has made the drug menace a major election issue. The party has been targeting the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its handling of the problem. Union home minister Amit Shah has even promised to make Punjab "drug-free" by December 2029 if the BJP comes to power.But AAP has hit back. Its national convener Arvind Kejriwal questioned the BJP over the drug problem in states where it is in power, including Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa, asking why the same deadline had not been set for them.The political exchange has also put the focus on Bihar, where alcohol has been banned for a decade but recent drug seizures have raised fresh concerns. More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections were seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026, while investigations have uncovered heroin consignments, codeine-based cough syrup and networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.But what do these seizures actually reveal? Is Bihar witnessing a rise in drug consumption, or is the state increasingly becoming a transit route for narcotics headed elsewhere? And has a decade of prohibition had any bearing on the availability and use of other intoxicants? Here's what the data revealsMore than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026.A sharp rise in smack seizures. Growing quantities of codeine-based cough syrup being intercepted. Across Bihar, recent drug seizures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape, raising questions about what is entering the state, where it is going and who is using it.But do these seizures signal a growing drug problem within Bihar, or are they exposing the scale of a trafficking network that uses the state as a transit route? Police have traced consignments from the Northeast and Nepal-linked routes, while investigations in Patna have uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.The answers are not straightforward. Five years of seizure data show sharp fluctuations rather than a consistent rise across substances. Meanwhile, a debate over Bihar’s liquor prohibition has raised another question about whether the use of alternative intoxicants has changed since the ban came into force in 2016.What do the numbers reveal?Bihar’s drug seizure data over five years shows that ganja accounted for the largest quantities seized among the major narcotics listed, while seizures of heroin fluctuated sharply. Ganja seizures rose from 16,607 kg in 2020 to 33,603 kg in 2021, before falling to 23,023 kg in 2022 and 13,129 kg in 2023. They increased again to 18,356 kg in 2024.Heroin seizures fell from 363.77 kg in 2020 to 9.62 kg in 2021, before rising to 31.13 kg in 2022, 27.37 kg in 2023 and 53.35 kg in 2024. Hashish seizures also varied, peaking at 395.12 kg in 2021 before declining to 195 kg in 2024.A person whose circle consumes drugs said, on the condition of anonymity, that marijuana remained the most widely consumed substance in their social circle and that they had not noticed a significant shift in preferences towards other drugs.“In most circles, marijuana is most widely consumed, and I don't think synthetic drugs have made their way to Bihar,” the person said.The data records smaller seizures of other substances, including ATS, cocaine and LSD in certain years. While these figures show fluctuations in the quantities of narcotics seized, they do not establish a steady year-on-year rise in drug trafficking or consumption. Seizure figures reflect what enforcement agencies intercept and, on their own, cannot establish how many people use drugs or whether drug abuse is increasing in Bihar.Police say a significant share of narcotics reaching Patna comes from the Northeast. The routes and methods of transportation vary according to the size of a consignment.Investigations have also pointed to supply chains passing through multiple states. In September, four people were arrested near JP Setu in Patna with 274 gm of heroin. Police traced the consignment to Assam, from where it allegedly travelled to Tamkuhi in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, before being sent towards Patna.Bihar’s location along the Nepal border adds another dimension to the problem. On October 25, Motihari Police, in a joint operation with the Bihar Special Task Force, seized smack valued at Rs 4 crore near Raxaul, close to the India-Nepal border.In a separate operation, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence’s Muzaffarpur unit and the Bihar STF busted a suspected network involved in smuggling Nepal-origin charas into India. Two people were arrested and 5.14 kg of charas, valued by officials at Rs 5.14 crore, was seized. Investigators said the consignment was intended for onward transportation to Indore in Madhya Pradesh.The cases point to Bihar’s role as a route for narcotics moving between regions. However, seizures along transport corridors do not establish how much of the intercepted supply is consumed within the state.Police investigations suggest that local networks are also involved in storage, preparation and distribution.In March, police found a rented room in Patna’s Ramakrishna Nagar area allegedly being used to prepare smack. A flat in Alamganj was allegedly used for distribution. Police recovered 1.68 kg of brown sugar and cash, along with cheques worth around Rs 70 lakh issued in the name of a police officer.The trade is not confined to substances traditionally associated with narcotics smuggling. Pharmaceutical products have also featured in investigations. In May, the DRI seized 7,500 bottles of codeine-based cough syrup from a pickup van outside Patna’s Rajendra Nagar Terminal. Investigators found that the consignee’s drug licence had been cancelled and that the firm did not exist at its stated address.Such cases raise questions about how pharmaceutical products enter illicit supply chains, how they are distributed and whether existing monitoring systems are able to detect diversion from legitimate channels.A Patna high court order has raised questions about how narcotics can travel long distances before being intercepted.In an order dated September 15, the court expressed concern over two minor boys who had travelled from Assam to Bihar in a car without a registration certificate. The vehicle was intercepted near Patna, and the directorate of revenue intelligence recovered more than 60 kg of cannabis from a concealed compartment.The court questioned how the vehicle had travelled uninterrupted from Assam to Bihar while carrying a commercial quantity of cannabis.Has prohibition changed pattern of substance use?Bihar banned the sale and consumption of alcohol in April 2016 under a policy introduced by the Nitish Kumar government. The prohibition was intended, among other objectives, to reduce domestic violence and encourage households to spend money on more productive needs.A research paper by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), titled Macro Perspective of Bihar's Development Achievements, Unfinished Agenda, and the Way Forward, has questioned whether the ban achieved its intended outcomes.The paper said reported crimes against women had not declined following prohibition and that total reported crimes against women increased over the post-2016 period. It also pointed to concerns about the expansion of illicit liquor trade, enforcement challenges, corruption and the use of alternative intoxicants, including illicit drugs."In tandem, there was a significant rise in illegal liquor trade leading to higher alcohol consumption, increased crime and corruption, and an increase in the use of alternative additive substances, such as illicit drugs," the paper said.The authors argued that Bihar should reconsider prohibition and restore alcohol excise duty to historical levels. They estimated that doing so could increase the state’s own revenues by 14-15%.Some residents also believe prohibition may be one factor behind the availability of other intoxicants, although personal accounts cannot establish a direct link between the ban and drug consumption.“I would argue that it is a byproduct of the prohibition in the state, but that isn't the full picture,” another person who spoke on condition of anonymity said, referring to the perceived increase in drug availability.The person said their observations were based on the experiences of people in their social circle who use drugs, adding that young people and those in their 30s appeared to be among the users they had noticed.“In a state like Bihar, with a large chunk of youth population that haven't so far been backed with job opportunities, [this] has also contributed to the rise of drug consumption in the state,” the person said.They also flagged a lack of awareness about addiction and the support available to people who use drugs.“I feel like there is a lack of awareness against remedial methods, like what to do if someone you know has become addicted to drugs, what are you supposed to do then. I feel like there is a lack of rehabilitation system and awareness among the people needed to curb the drug menace,” the person said.The distinction matters because seizures measure what enforcement agencies intercept, not the total volume of drugs entering the market or being consumed.Bihar’s prohibition and narcotics enforcement policies also form part of a wider debate over how the state measures the effectiveness of its policing. A rise in seizures can reflect an increase in trafficking, improved detection or a combination of both.Bihar minister Madan Sahni has rejected the charge that rising seizures indicate a failure of prohibition. He said the increase was not confined to Bihar but was a phenomenon seen in other states as well."I must say that due to the alertness of the officials concerned, the quantity of the seizure of substances prohibited under the NDPS Act has increased in the state, but at the same time, people should know that the majority of the prohibited substances seized in Bihar are meant for supply to other states," he said.Sahni added that intercepting consignments within Bihar could create the impression that the drugs were intended for local consumption, even when they were being transported elsewhere. He also defended prohibition, saying it had been successful.The minister’s argument points to an important gap in the available figures. Without comparable data on drug use, treatment demand, drug-related health emergencies and the destinations of intercepted consignments, it is difficult to determine how much of the rise reflects local consumption.RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, meanwhile, cited a media report and said the situation was out of control."An entire generation has been ruined. This is what happens when the government has no control. The situation here is completely out of control..." he said.Bihar’s recent seizure figures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape. Police have reported sharp increases in some categories, identified supply routes running through several states and uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparation and distribution. Seizures near the Nepal border have also highlighted the state’s role in cross-border trafficking.But the central question remains unresolved. Is Bihar facing a growing drug-consumption problem, a trafficking problem that extends beyond its borders, or both?
Article Summary: NCB destroyed 1,170.15 kg of seized narcotics worth Rs 4.54 crore in Patna, Bihar, across four cases to prevent their recirculation in September. More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections were seized in the first eight months of 2026, while investigations have uncovered heroin consignments, codeine-based cough syrup and networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) decision-making process amid allegations that key decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken without the unanimous consent."We know everything. We will examine," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the poll panel, Live Law reported.The three-judge bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, adjourned the hearing to November 17.The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECI’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous.The CJI's remark came after senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for leader of opposition on Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, urged the court to direct the ECI to preserve file notings and internal communications related to its decisions.Singhvi argued that the records were crucial to determining whether the decisions concerning the SIR were taken unanimously or unilaterally."This whole issue depends on the decision-making process, consultation, and whether the decision was unanimous or not unanimous.Let file notings, etc be preserved," Singhvi added.The petitions challenge the functioning of Gyanesh Kumar alleged that several ECI decisions, including those related to the SIR, were issued without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners.The bench also issued notices to the ECI and other respondents on a fresh petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen. The plea alleges that changes were made to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR without the Supreme Court’s approval.Senior advocate and MP Maneka Guruswamy, appearing for Sen, told the court that the poll panel had wrongly claimed that the changes to Form 6 were approved by the top court.The CJI said the court would examine all the issues and asked senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the first petitioner, Rakesh Kumar Singh to file a rejoinder within 10 days to the ECI’s reply affidavit.Earlier on Monday, in its 248-page affidavit, the ECI strongly defended the SIR and rejected allegations that Form 6, the statutory form used for voter registration, had been amended."The attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate," the affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the ECI said, PTI reported.The poll panel also maintained that no changes had been made to the statutory Form 6. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing through a unanimous decision of all three Election Commissioners.The petitions followed a report published by The Indian Express on September 25, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the preceding 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR.According to the report, the two commissioners had objected that the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The allegations triggered protests by opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The Supreme Court will take up the matter again on November 17, after the petitioners file their rejoinders to the ECI's affidavit.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India's decision-making process. The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECI’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous.

NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the BJP The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state. However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his “mistake” of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves."We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party. The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed. "The timing and context of Jagan’s remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his “solo” politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congress’s biggest Achilles heel across states.Jagan Mohan Reddy’s MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jagan’s help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha. The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha.Despite being spurned by the BJP and his party’s shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. After all, he still had 15 MPs (4 in Lok Sabha and 11 in Rajya Sabha) to provide the much-needed support to the BJP’s minority government at the Centre. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest.But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naidu’s support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy. Nearly two and a half years down the line, Reddy seems to have accepted this harsh reality and is perhaps gearing up to chart a new path for the next political challenge in 2029.However, for any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page. And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy.Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jagan’s supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister. The Congress leadership did not approve of Jagan’s Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his father’s death.That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career.In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the party’s declining political fortunes in the state.On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies. The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congress’s vote share was reduced to less than 1%.The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddy’s sister Y S Sharmila as part of the party’s revival plan. Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024.However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jagan’s electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats. The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt.And that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jagan’s remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open “regret” for backing the BJP.But does this “open regret” mean an olive branch for the Congress?Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy.“Politics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father. So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,” Sanjay Jha says.However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. “Once a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry. The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,” Sanjay Jha adds.The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy.This is easier said than done. The Congress has a poor track record when it comes to winning back states it has lost. We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it.In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. Naidu’s call for greater cooperation and coordination among southern states at a recent conference is perhaps an effort to keep his importance and relevance intact. We saw DMK’s MK Stalin make similar moves before he lost power to Vijay’s TVK in the last assembly elections.Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress face an uphill electoral battle in 2029. It will be interesting to see if they can agree to an alliance to take on Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP.
Article Summary: Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament. For any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page.

Article Title: Who named Cyclone Arnab and why? Where it will hit, states on alert and preparedness
Article Text:
Rough sea conditions prevail ahead of the expected landfall, in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh

Why is it named Arnab? How storm naming works

Andhra Pradesh braces for landfall

Odisha, Jharkhand face heavy rain, strong winds

West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh also likely to see unseasonal rain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is bracing for Cyclone Arnab as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected by Wednesday forenoon as authorities expect strong winds, heavy rainfall and possible flooding across several states. Cyclone Arnab is drawing attention not only for its projected impact along the Andhra Pradesh coast but also for its name.Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph, when the storm crosses the coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. Its effects are expected in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, prompting weather alerts and precautionary measures.The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. It is pronounced “Ornab”.Cyclone names in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea are assigned by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)/United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Panel on Tropical Cyclones. The naming system began in 2004, with the list subsequently expanded as more countries joined the panel.The current list contains 52 names contributed by 13 countries: Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. The list was adopted in April 2020.Names are used sequentially, column-wise, according to the established list. Each name is used only once and is not repeated in subsequent lists. The Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, operated by the IMD, is responsible for naming cyclones that form over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea once they reach the prescribed intensity.Naming storms helps meteorological agencies, governments, disaster management authorities and the public identify and communicate warnings about individual weather systems more easily.The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, moving west-northwestwards before its expected turn towards the coast. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has warned of heavy rainfall in northern coastal districts, including Srikakulam, with strong winds already affecting parts of the coast.Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas, as potentially vulnerable. According to the state disaster management authorities, 1,763 cyclone shelters have been readied, 2,907 control rooms established and 3,185 nodal officers deployed. National and state disaster response teams have also been positioned in 11 high-risk districts.Authorities have banned public access to beaches and announced restrictions on coastal road movement. Fishing vessels have been secured at harbours, with the APSDMA saying 30,043 fishing vessels have been anchored.Air India has warned that adverse weather could affect flights to and from Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada on October 27. Passengers have been advised to check their flight status and allow additional time for travel to airports. Ashwini Vaishnaw said safety protocols and rapid restoration measures were in place across the Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions ahead of Cyclone Arnab’s expected landfall on October 28. In a post on X, he said war rooms were active at zonal, divisional and Railway Board levels, with around 600 km of track under close watch. “Passenger safety is the top priority,” Vaishnaw said, adding that relief wagons, diesel locomotives, ambulances and restoration equipment had been stationed at key locations, while wind speeds and water levels were being monitored hourly. He also said coordination with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and state disaster authorities was under way.Odisha has already experienced heavy rain and strong winds in parts of the state. The IMD has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall, ranging from 12 cm to 20 cm, in Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. A yellow warning has been issued for several other districts.Tourist boat and ferry operations at Chilika Lake have been suspended from October 26 to 29 as a precaution. Authorities have moved boats to safer locations, while Paradip Port has provided shelter to 305 fishermen at its Eastern Quay-1 berth.In Jharkhand, the state government has directed district administrations to remain vigilant. A yellow alert for heavy rain has been issued for several districts on October 28, followed by orange alerts for parts of the state through October 30. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected.The Ranchi district administration has warned of waterlogging, overflowing drains and water bodies, damage to weak structures and possible flood-like conditions in low-lying areas. Standing crops could also be affected by water accumulation.The cyclone's influence is expected to extend to West Bengal between October 28 and 30. In south Bengal, heavy rainfall is forecast in South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura and Paschim Bardhaman on October 28 and 29. Kolkata is likely to receive light to moderate rain over the next 48 hours.In the sub-Himalayan region, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri are likely to experience heavy rain on October 29 and 30. The IMD has also advised fishermen not to venture into the sea until October 29, warning of rough to very rough conditions and squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, along and off the West Bengal coast.Uttar Pradesh is forecast to receive unseasonal rain, thunderstorms and strong winds between October 28 and 31. The IMD has issued alerts for several districts, with heavy rain possible in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Awadh and the Terai region. Daytime temperatures could fall by 5-8 degrees Celsius in some areas on October 30.Authorities have advised residents to follow official weather bulletins, avoid unnecessary travel during storms and stay away from trees, electricity poles, weak structures and open fields during lightning.
Article Summary: The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, moving west-northwestwards before its expected turn towards the coast. Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas as potentially vulnerable.
