The reason for defeating Dr Sanjayan Tripathi through vote-counting irregularities is not merely that he is an SP candidate; the main reason behind it is “Haata nahi bhaata” (he is not acceptable to them). In matters of politics, the BJP has sunk to the lowest depths. After such massive fraud, the public has realised that the BJP has, in fact, lost every seat," he wrote."BJP leaders win not through votes, but through foul means," former UP CM added.Targeting the BJP over its alleged treatment of teachers, the SP chief said the incident had left a deep impression on Tripathi's community and teachers across the state.“The way Sanjayan Tripathi has been harassed is being witnessed by his entire community. Neither his community nor any teacher in the state will forget Dr. Tripathi's tears,” the SP chief said, alleging that teachers had received nothing but humiliation from the BJP government.Akhilesh also linked the controversy to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, claiming that teachers would remember the alleged mistreatment when they vote.“Every teacher will always remember the despicable conspiracy to make teachers do the unwanted task of collecting fodder, and will fulfil their “guru resolve” by defeating the BJP in the 2027 assembly elections,” he wrote.Taking another swipe at the ruling party, Akhilesh said its alleged electoral tactics would not succeed across the state."The BJP's “400 BC” (a pun on char sau beesi, meaning fraud or deceit) will not work across all 403 seats," he further said.Reiterating his support for Tripathi, the SP chief added, "We stand with Sanjayan Tripathi and against every injustice and act of harassment inflicted upon him and his community. We stand united against the BJP and will continue to do so."The remarks came amid allegations of irregularities during the counting of votes for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Division Teachers' constituency. SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi and independent candidate Rajeev Yadav boycotted the counting process, accusing administrative officials and the election observer of favouring the BJP candidate.Speaking to news agency ANI, Tripathi alleged that the counting trend changed abruptly after the first three rounds, when independent candidate Rajeev Yadav was leading by around 450 votes.“We have boycotted the vote-counting process. Everything was proceeding smoothly for the first three rounds of counting; independent candidate Rajiv Yadav was leading by approximately 450 votes. Suddenly, the counting began to shift entirely in favour of the BJP candidate; the trend changed abruptly, making it appear as though the outcome had been predetermined. Consequently, we decided to boycott the process,” Tripathi said.He also alleged police misconduct and claimed that the authorities were determined to ensure the ruling party's candidate won.A day earlier, Akhilesh had urged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to take immediate cognisance of the alleged irregularities and ensure transparency in the counting process. He had accused officials of delaying the announcement of round-wise results and warned that the SP would launch a movement and file a case against the Election Commission if any foul play was detected.Similar allegations were raised by SP candidate Danish Akhtar over the results in the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' constituency. Akhtar alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls and voting process, claiming that 30 per cent of the names on the electoral roll were fraudulent. He also accused the Election Commission of failing to act despite receiving evidence and repeated representations.Meanwhile, in Lucknow, Ram Singh Rana, an SP agent for party candidate Kanti Singh, claimed on Wednesday that the party was maintaining its lead during counting. He alleged that BJP candidate Avnish Singh had repeatedly attempted to disrupt the process.“We have been steadily increasing our lead since yesterday, and it continues to grow. The opposition candidate from the BJP made several attempts to misuse power, but the Samajwadi youth did not bow down; they stood firm and remained unafraid--even when there were lathi-charges during the night, and chairs were smashed,” Rana said.Rana alleged that the opposition had tried to halt the counting process four or five times and that SP workers had faced harassment throughout the night."The opposition tried to halt the process four or five times, but no one gave in or felt intimidated. We have maintained our momentum and are moving toward victory. We faced harassment all night long. The opposition candidate, Avnish Singh, tried to stop the process five times, but we did not back down," Rana said.Sharing the vote figures after four rounds of counting, Rana said Kanti Singh had secured 25,382 votes, while the BJP candidate had received 17,797 votes.“As the counting for the fifth round begins, the margin is significant, and we are continuing to pull further ahead,” he added.Polling for five Graduates' constituencies and six Teachers' constituencies in Uttar Pradesh concluded on October 23, with counting held on October 27.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav accuses Bharatiya Janata Party of electoral malpractice. Alleges irregularities during counting were part of a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi. Targeting the BJP over its alleged treatment of teachers, the SP chief said the incident had left a deep impression on Tripathi's community.

Article Title: 'Process becomes punishment in our system': Ex-SC judge Sanjay Kaul on Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam bail pleas
Article Text:
Ex-SC judge Justice Kaul flags ‘punishment’ of prolonged custody before conviction

‘Met him only a couple of times’: Justice Kaul on Saurav Das

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said that the period before conviction or acquittal has become a "punishment" in India, commenting on the denial of bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam . He said that prolonged legal proceedings can themselves become a form of punishment and that bail should generally be the norm.In an interview with news agency ANI, Kaul said he had generally taken a liberal view on bail, but acknowledged that certain laws explicitly restrict the granting of bail in specific cases."I have taken a generally very liberal view on bail. I feel the bail cannot be the punishment. The conviction is the punishment. In our system, unfortunately, the pre-conviction or acquittal period itself becomes a punishment. The process becomes a punishment," former Supreme Court judge said.Kaul said several judges had raised concerns about the issue. He also referred to a judgment written by Justice Sundaresh, with whom he had dealt with the question of bail and the principles governing custody."And many judges have been writing and talking about it. In fact, I, sitting with Justice Sundaresh, had dealt elaborately with the bail itself, trying to say, why are you people under custody? Justice Sundaresh wrote the judgment.He's, to my mind, a liberal judge on this. And we tried to lay down norms, etc., which were already in existence, but trying to, you know, until this case. So in most cases, our view is, that bail should be the norm. But there are certain acts which prohibit bail," said Kaul.Kaul has co-authored an upcoming memoir, Without Fear or Favour, with Jay Vinayak Ojha. The book is scheduled for release on October 31.Khalid and Imam are accused under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in connection with an alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. According to the prosecution, the violence left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.The riots broke out amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, and the proposed National Register of Citizens.On January 5 this year, the Supreme Court denied bail to Khalid and Imam in the case related to the alleged conspiracy behind the 2020 riots. In its judgment, the court observed that the two accused stood on a "qualitatively different footing" in terms of the prosecution's case and the evidence against them.In September, the Delhi high court had also rejected their bail pleas. The case stems from FIR 59/2020, registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell to investigate the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Meanwhile, former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul also clarified his association with Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das, saying he had met him only a couple of times when Das was working as a journalist and had advised him to "taper down a little" in his language.Justice Kaul told news agency ANI that a photograph of him with Das, taken at a Diwali gathering about a year ago, was being used to suggest that he shared a particular ideology."So, it was one year ago. He was not even in the news then," Justice Kaul said, explaining how the meeting came about."He was a journalist, maybe met me a couple of times. He was insistent that I must, at Diwali time, come. I was going somewhere else. I said, 'Okay, I'll drop in for ten minutes.' I told my wife, 'Have a cup of coffee, I'll drop in for ten minutes, and then we'll go.' That's all that happened," he said.Asked whether he had mentored Das at any point, Justice Kaul denied doing so, while acknowledging that he had advised the activist on his choice of words."I was not mentoring him, but once or twice he met me, I told him that, I will always tell you to taper down a little in your language," he said.Justice Kaul added that differences in language and expression across generations could sometimes cause discomfort, particularly among those accustomed to more civil forms of conversation.
Article Summary: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul says prolonged legal proceedings can themselves become a form of punishment. Kaul said he had generally taken a liberal view on bail, but acknowledged that certain laws explicitly restrict the granting of bail in specific cases. He also clarified his association with Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das.

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday deputed a high-level team to investigation the death of a 19-month-old male Cheetah of Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, caused by firearm pellet injuries.The team has been tasked with undertaking a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of the Cheetah, examining all available evidence and coordinating closely with the Madhya Pradesh forest department to ensure strict and swift action in the matter.The 19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park. Preliminary medical examinations corroborated multiple internal injuries associated with the firearm pellets.The incident, the first reported casualty of a shooting since PM Narendra Modi launched Project Cheetah at Kuno in Sept, 2022, is being viewed quite seriously at the Centre, given the critical importance of Project Cheetah and the need to ensure the highest standards of protection for the reintroduced population of the Big Cat.“As reported by the MP forest department, the injured cheetah was rescued from the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division the same day and provided intensive veterinary care and emergency surgery at the veterinary facility in Jabalpur. During the surgery, five firearm pellets were recovered from its body. Despite the medical intervention, the Cheetah succumbed to its injuries on Oct 27,” said the Union environment ministry in a statement.It said, “The state govt has already constituted a Special Task Force (STF), comprising forest and police officers, to investigate the incident. The central team deputed by the Union environment ministry would work in coordination with the state machinery. It would also examine the implementation of security protocols, as well as monitoring and protection measures being undertaken to avoid any such incident in future.“The central team would submit its findings and recommendations to the ministry for further directions to the state govt and field authorities.”The central team comprises the Inspector General of Forests, National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), Additional Director, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), and Regional Deputy Director, WCCB.
Article Summary: 19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park. Five firearm pellets were recovered from its body.

Article Title: UAE honours flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who fought off co-pilot’s attack to save passengers
Article Text:
UAE honours Indian flydubai pilot for thwarting mid-air attack

NEW DELHI: The UAE has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew of flydubai Flight FZ1073 for their courage in protecting passengers during a serious in-flight incident. UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First-Class Order of Zayed II on the crew on Tuesday.The honour was presented by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, in the presence of UAE Vice President, Prime Minister and Dubai Ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, also met the crew members on Tuesday.On September 30, Flight FZ1073, operating from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia following a serious incident in the cockpit. Captain Machchhar was injured, while crew members, off-duty pilots and passengers helped bring the situation under control. The aircraft landed safely, and all 172 passengers and crew were reported safe.During the meeting, the UAE leaders praised the crew for their courage and sense of responsibility in protecting passengers. They stressed that human safety and security remain the UAE's highest priority.While Machchhar was receiving treatment for his injuries, Sheikh Hamdan visited him and praised his courage, sense of responsibility and commitment to protecting human life.The deputy prime minister expressed pride in Machchhar being part of the "story of our nation"."During a visit to Captain Smit Machchhar… the flydubai pilot who embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise. We are proud that he is part of our team… part of the story of our nation… and part of what the UAE stands for… a nation of compassion… a nation of peace… and a nation of life," he wrote in a post on X.In an earlier interview with the UAE's state-owned newspaper The National, Machchhar recalled the attack by the co-pilot and said he suffered several blows before he could open the cockpit door.“The first time when I was hit … my thought was something's gone horribly wrong with the aircraft structure, which has fallen on my head. It almost made me fall on my control column. In the next couple of seconds, when the hits kept on coming, (I realised) it was the other person who I thought was supposed to be on the team.”“My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts. And I tried to just block the blows as much as I could, because the blows were coming on the head… While the first few blows came in, my vision … it was so narrow. I lost a lot. I was just looking (at) outlines,” he told The National.“Immediately, my hand went to the knob which opens the door. And (I was) screaming for my colleagues. I believe that was the first time when I lost consciousness. I fell face down in the cockpit,” he added.Recalling the moment when the aircraft plunged 17,000 feet, Machchhar said, “The scariest thing that I heard and felt was the engines spooling down.”Despite the attack, Machchhar said his love for flying remained unchanged.“Did my love die for aviation? Not at all. Not at all. I'm just glad that I was able to do my part.”Machchhar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot. The co-pilot had attacked him with an axe in an attempt to bring down the aircraft. A hijacking distress signal was also sent.The flight was diverted to Tabuk, where it made an emergency landing with the help of passengers who helped land the aircraft. All 180 occupants disembarked without injury, according to the account of the incident.Israeli President Isaac Herzog has also announced that he would confer Israel's Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism on Machchhar.
Article Summary: The UAE has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew of flydubai Flight FZ1073. UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First- Class Order of Zayed II on the crew on Tuesday. The co-pilot had attacked him with an axe in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.

New Delhi: Candidates allotted postgraduate medical seats under NEET-PG counselling 2026 are facing difficulties completing the online joining process, with some reporting that nodal officers listed on the official portal are unreachable or their contact details are invalid.At Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital, candidates have complained that the nodal officer’s mobile phone is switched off and landline numbers are not reachable. Candidates have also flagged similar difficulties with the University College of Medical Sciences (UCMS), where the portal displays a nodal officer’s mobile number as “00000000”, making it impossible to contact the designated official on that number. We will also raise the matter in a meeting and seek a resolution.”The issue assumes significance for candidates who have opted for the float option in counselling. Those choosingaccept the allotted seat, while candidates choosingwish to retain their current allotment while remaining eligible for an upgrade in subsequent rounds. Candidates who have to complete online reporting and submit documents are seeking timely verification and clear communication from their allotted institutes.The MCC portal itself displays a message stating that document verification is pending at the allotted institute and advises candidates to contact the nodal officer for admission-related queries. But when the listed contact details do not work, candidates are left without a clear channel to resolve their concerns.A social media post by a former J&K nodal officer for the Diplomate of National Board (DNB) programme also raised questions over outdated contact details. He said an MCC allotment letter dated October 23 listed his name and personal mobile number as the J&K nodal officer despite his having retired.Candidates say delays or confusion over document verification can leave them uncertain about whether their joining formalities have been completed within the prescribed timeline. They want the MCC and participating colleges to ensure that contact details are current, officials are reachable and admission-related queries are addressed promptly.The complaints raise questions about who is accountable for coordinating online joining during counselling, and what recourse candidates have when neither the college nor the helpline can resolve their queries.

NEW DELHI: India reiterated at the UN that as long as the veto power exists in the Security Council, it must be held by all permanent members of a reformed council and not just the current countries.While the veto issue may arise only in case of any new permanent member that may be admitted, India’s position always has been that there should be no discrimination in the Security Council and also no second class of permanent members without veto.“Fairness and justice demand that all permanent members enjoy the same rights and responsibilities.” said Indian ambassador to the UN P Haish while participating in a debate in the UNGA on the veto question.“India’s position on the veto is principled and well known.... Article Summary: India reiterated at the UN that as long as the veto power exists in the Security Council, it must be held by all permanent members of a reformed council. Article Title: Need to balance right to free speech, privacy: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Right to free speech of media needs balancing with privacy of citizens: SC

Privacy act will hit freedom of Press: Digital news body

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC on Tuesday acknowledged the importance of media’s right to freedom of speech and expression but said this needed to be balanced with citizens’ right to privacy and dignity and asked petitioner Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) to suggest how these two rights could coexist harmoniously.Entertaining DNPA’s petition terming certain provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the amendment to RTI Act redefining ‘personal information’ as an attempt towards pre-censorship of news content that violated the media’s right to free speech and impeded media independence, SC said, “You are domain experts. You suggest to the govt and SC how to harmonise the two competing rights.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymlaya Bagchi and V Mohana said: “Media must ensure there is no misuse of the rights enjoyed by it. There must be a balance between your rights and the rights of innocent citizens. We will have to leave it to you to suggest how best you are going to ensure that the media’s rights are not misused and the right to privacy of citizens are not violated.”Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Madhavi Divan said provisions of DPDP Act failed to provide exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class and had brought the regime of notice and prior consent within it, which would lead to closure of newsrooms as they feed live information.If journalists went around seeking consent of people, then no news could be disseminated, she said.“It is not merely the fundamental right to speech and expression and dissemination of information owing to freedom of the press which has been set at nought by the aforesaid provision, but the DPDP Act places myriad restrictions in the manner in which information is accessed, processed and disseminated,” DNPA said.“In the absence of exemptions, the entire scheme under Chapter II of DPDP Act will constitute unreasonable restrictions upon journalists in the exercise of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression and practise any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business,” it added.The petitioner complained that DPDP Act imposed onerous conditions governing how information was to be disseminated and how access was obtained and cited an SC judgement, which had ruled that the fundamental right to know could not be sacrificed at the altar of privacy.The bench issued notice to the Centre on the petition and tagged it with a clutch of petitions which are scheduled for hearing on Nov 17.
Article Summary: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and amendment to RTI Act redefining ‘personal information’ were cited as an attempt towards pre-censorship of news content. SC asked petitioner Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) to suggest how these two rights could coexist harmoniously.

NEW DELHI: General medicine accounted for more allotments than radiodiagnosis among top entries in the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, highlighting the competing career attractions of the two sought-after PG specialties, reports Anuja Jaiswal.An analysis of Medical Counselling Committee’s Round 1 allotment list shows 51 allotments in general medicine as against 28 in radiodiagnosis among the first 100 entries. Dermatology was a distant third with six allotments, while paediatrics and general surgery had three each. Doctors say the choices reflect different career priorities. Radiology attracts candidates because of its good work-life balance.Radiology attracts candidates because of its prospect of earning well early in their careers. General medicine, on the other hand, remains an evergreen specialty, offering opportunities to pursue super-specialisation and earn more in the long run. However, financial settlement can take longer, as candidates must complete a DM course and then build their practice, which could take another two to three years.“General medicine appeals to candidates who enjoy clinical challenges, patient interaction and managing complex diseases.While the financial rewards may take longer to materialise, the scope for super-specialisation and professional growth is immense. Ultimately, the choice should be guided by what fulfils you as a doctor, not just by how quickly you can start earning,” said Prof Neeraj Nischal, internal medicine, AIIMS.According to a senior doctor, radiology is attractive because it offers good earning potential early in one’s career. However, with AI advancing rapidly, some candidates may also be weighing the technology’s long-term impact on the specialty.While this does not mean that human expertise will not be needed, the growing role of AI could influence how students assess radiology as a career choice.
Article Summary: General medicine accounted for more allotments than radiodiagnosis among top entries in the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. Doctors say the choices reflect different career priorities. Radiology attracts candidates because of its good work-life balance. General medicine remains an evergreen specialty, offering opportunities to pursue super-specialisation.

Article Title: Government working on bill to curb child & revenge porn: Solicitor general in SC
Article Text:
Government told the Supreme Court it is drafting a bill to prevent circulation of child pornography and offensive sexual videos online

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday informed Supreme Court it is in the process of drafting a bill to prevent social media circulation of child pornography, vindictive uploading of videos of consensual sexual acts after souring of relations, morphing of videos to ridicule or defame personalities, and permitting any person to file police complaint against such offensive contents.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deliberations are on for legislative intervention to prevent circulation of sexual contents, child porn and morphed videos on social media.Mehta said he is not opposing the two PILs, one by Uday Mahurkar and another by NGO ‘Prajwala’, both of which seek robust mechanism to stop circulation of child pornography, sexual assault videos, uploading of videos of consensual adult sexual acts by jilted lovers and morphed videos.When a counsel said at present only the aggrieved person, in most cases women, can file police complaints against the person uploading such videos, the SG said the intermediary should not only be directed to immediately take down such offensive contents but also mandatorily file police complaint against the handle or digital device from which such contents were uploaded.The bench agreed that a robust legislative intervention would be required to stop the menace. It gave govt four weeks to inform the court about the outcome of the ongoing deliberations.
Article Summary: Government told the Supreme Court it is drafting a bill to prevent circulation of child pornography and offensive sexual videos online. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deliberations are on.
